correctness.rationale: Rooted PD is a sum of clade-intersection indicators. Inclusion-exclusion yields exact first/second moments; a binomial-coefficient triangular transform proves exact equivalence with the size/union-size spectrum. Equal-four-subtree swapping preserves that signature by a complete classification of edge pairs; 16-tip witnesses differ in topological shape. A canonical induction generates and checks all 10,905 16-tip shapes and all smaller shapes, finding the unique 16-tip collision; exact enumeration of 120 tip pairs gives third-moment gap minus one twentieth. Root grafting preserves the signature for every larger n. The finite exhaustive lower bound and infinite grafting proof are independent arguments.

originality.rationale: Published rarefaction results establish general moment formulas and tree-balance work establishes clade-size mean-only ambiguity already at nine tips. They do not cover the sharp simultaneous first/second-moment ambiguity at sixteen tips, its unique first pair, its third-moment separation or its persistence at all larger sizes by equal-size swaps. Relevant topical searches and direct primary texts revealed no implying theorem; remaining risk is unidentified broader algebraic/combinatorial treatment.
residual_risks: A prior tree-shape identifiability statement phrased via equal clade-size and pair-union spectra might subsume the exact 16-tip boundary but was not located.
The 16-tip minimality is a finite exhaustive computer-assisted argument, not a short purely symbolic classification.
The sharp cutoff does not extend without proof to arbitrary branch lengths, unrooted PD or nonbinary trees.

value.rationale: Faith-style rooted PD under uniform rarefaction is used to summarize sampled evolutionary biodiversity. The exact earliest topology collision for the entire mean-and-variance curves measures how much shape information survives two standard summaries. The result has a unique sharp sixteen-tip counterexample, an exact higher-moment remedy for that pair, and an analytic obstruction for all larger sizes; these properties are not routine substitutions into a known formula.
